proposedRule.label: NEW — proposed for owner review; not accepted or operative

eligibility.subject: An active Mage at Mage class level 10 or higher whose pre-transformation mechanical creature-type set is exactly ["Humanoid"], with lawful access to a level-10 Lich Hero-path acquisition opportunity under the bound progression, and who does not already have Undead. Mage level 10 alone does not grant a second Hero path or authorize respec; any later acquisition or respec requires its own accepted source or a separately labeled NEW rule.
readiness: Obtain either one Soul Coin or two ritual participants.
Bind at least two named mini-bosses as guardians.
existingModifiers: A third bound guardian grants +2 to the final ritual check.
If both ritual participants are willing, the final ritual check has advantage.
eligibility.accessAndTiming: This is a NEW timing and scheduling proposal, not an existing source rule and not derived from any short-rest rule. All lawful Mage-level, Hero-path acquisition and ritual-readiness requirements must be true before the final ritual step begins and rechecked immediately before the final roll. The final Lich ritual step occupies one continuous 60-minute elapsed-world-time interval at the secured planar nexus. It is a scheduled ritual activity, not a spell cast or regular Action; it grants no turn, Action, Reaction, resource refresh or paused clock, and the Mage cannot take another voluntary activity during the interval. Explain the historical failure stakes and obtain explicit player opt-in before the interval begins; consent may be withdrawn before the final roll, which aborts the step without a check or failure consequence. The type addition applies once, only immediately after actual successful resolution of the final check; preparation, declaration, declining, interruption or failure never triggers it.

paymentAndConsumptionClarification.status: NEW proposal to make the existing readiness wording deterministic; requires separate owner review.
paymentAndConsumptionClarification.soulCoinRoute: NEW proposed ritual cost, separate from any taxonomy cost: the Soul Coin option is checked as an acquired and available readiness prerequisite before the ritual step and again immediately before the final roll. If the roll is attempted, one qualifying Soul Coin is committed and consumed immediately before the roll, whether the transformation succeeds or fails. If the step is interrupted before the roll, no coin is consumed. This is a proposed completion, not an inference from the word obtaining.
paymentAndConsumptionClarification.participantRoute: NEW proposed alternate route: two participants remain available to complete the ritual step; they are not consumed or killed by this proposal. If both are willing at the final check, apply the source-stated advantage. The participant route substitutes for the Soul Coin route; no additional RP, spell slot or material payment is added.
paymentAndConsumptionClarification.failureTiming: The selected Soul Coin is spent immediately before any final roll and is not refunded on a failed roll. The participant route incurs no consumable payment. Interruption before the roll consumes no coin and does not trigger the historical roll-failure outcome. All of these cost-timing clauses are NEW proposed mechanics pending separate owner review.
paymentAndConsumptionClarification.taxonomyCost: No separate cost is charged for adding Undead taxonomy; the ritual cost for the successful Lich transformation is distinct and is governed by the NEW proposed coin-or-participants terms above.

checkAndResolution.check: After all readiness gates and the divine-echo encounter are complete, roll d20 + Intelligence modifier + Constitution modifier against DC 20, applying the existing third-guardian +2 and willing-participant advantage where applicable.
checkAndResolution.successTiming: Immediately after successful resolution of the final check, add Undead to the same character's creature-type set. The type update is one atomic rules-state update; it does not create a second creature or body.
checkAndResolution.failure: The existing historical failure state and agreed player-to-NPC handoff remain unchanged. The proposed taxonomy addition does not occur on failure.

identityAndBodyMapping.identity: Preserve the same creature identity and character record.
identityAndBodyMapping.bodyAndLifeState: Continue the same extant body and same active creature life state; the character is alive, not a corpse. Do not create a replacement body, death, corpse, resurrection or separate creature.
identityAndBodyMapping.positionOrientationAndVolume: Preserve the exact position, orientation, occupied volume and current spatial relation before and after the type update. No movement, crossing, admission or cell transition occurs.
identityAndBodyMapping.hpConditionsEquipmentCargoAndCustody: This type update changes none of current HP, maximum HP, conditions, equipment, carried items, cargo ownership or custody.
identityAndBodyMapping.fitRequirement: Occupied volume is unchanged, so this proposed rule requires no changed-volume fit calculation and does not displace any creature or object.
identityAndBodyMapping.resourcesAndBudgets: The taxonomy addition itself changes no RP, Dissonance, class resources, turn/action budgets, rest counters or other resources.

taxonomyAndInteractions.duration: Propose permanent taxonomy after successful transformation, with no concentration requirement and no automatic expiry or reversion.
taxonomyAndInteractions.terminationAndReversion: Propose permanent taxonomy, with no concentration, automatic expiry or automatic reversion. Removal requires an expressly applicable accepted rule; this proposal grants no removal mechanism. The proposal does not invent a dispel, voluntary removal, death-state or reversion procedure.
taxonomyAndInteractions.targeting: A requirement for either Humanoid or Undead may qualify; an explicit exclusion of either excludes the character. All other targeting predicates remain necessary.
taxonomyAndInteractions.lifeState: Describe the result as the same active creature life state, not a corpse; do not exempt the character from Undead targeting.
taxonomyAndInteractions.setSemantics: Require exact initial set [Humanoid]. On success, add Undead while retaining Humanoid; no other pre-existing type is removed or rewritten.

abilitiesAndAcquisition.existingUnlocks: Preserve existing successful Lich path and elite-companion unlocks. Each card, companion and feature retains its printed acquisition and use requirements. Undead Immunities remains a separately selected Mage 16 card; taxonomy does not grant or accelerate it.

proposedRule.proposedInsertionText: NEW — proposed, not operative unless separately accepted: For an active Mage who lawfully acquires the Lich Hero path at a permitted level-10 Hero-path opportunity and whose pre-transformation type set is exactly [Humanoid], successful resolution of the bound Lich ritual adds Undead once while retaining Humanoid. No second Hero path or unsupported respec is granted. Apply only after the final check succeeds; preparation, declaration, decline, interruption and failure do not trigger this rule. Use the same active creature and extant body, preserving identity, ancestry, variant, position, orientation, occupied volume, HP, conditions, resources, equipment, cargo identities and custody. No death, corpse, resurrection, movement, replacement, duplication, crossing, admission or cell transition results. The proposed taxonomy is permanent, with no concentration, automatic expiry or automatic reversion; removal requires an expressly applicable accepted rule, and no removal mechanism is granted. A requirement for either Humanoid or Undead may qualify; an explicit exclusion of either excludes, with all other targeting predicates still required. Type membership alone grants no ancestry package, Lichborn traits, immunities, breathing/rest exemptions, resource recovery or unselected card; Undead Immunities remains separately selected at Mage 16. Existing ritual requirements and failure outcomes remain in force. Final ritual duration, scheduling, interruption, prerequisite recheck and cost timing are separately labeled NEW proposal terms and are not inferred from existing sources.

ritualTimingAndInterruption.status: NEW proposed terms requiring separate owner review; not an established Lich rule.
ritualTimingAndInterruption.scheduling: One continuous 60-minute scheduled activity at the secured planar nexus, measured on the ordinary elapsed-world-time clock. No initiative turn, Action, Reaction, spell casting, refresh or clock pause is created; the Mage is occupied and cannot take another voluntary activity.
ritualTimingAndInterruption.readinessRecheck: Check all level/path, readiness, nexus, bound-guardian, selected cost-route and consent conditions immediately before beginning and immediately before the final roll. Resolve +2 only if at least three named guardians remain bound at the final roll; apply advantage only if both ritual participants are actually willing then.
interruptions: Mage becomes incapacitated before the final roll.
Mage leaves or is forced away from the secured nexus ritual site.
The planar nexus ceases to be secured.
Fewer than two named mini-boss guardians remain bound.
The selected Soul Coin route no longer has one qualifying Soul Coin available immediately before the final roll.
The selected participant route no longer has two participants available to complete the ritual step.
The player withdraws explicit consent before the final roll.
ritualTimingAndInterruption.otherEvents: An event interrupts only if it meets one listed condition; damage alone does not interrupt unless it causes a listed condition. Ordinary world effects and clocks continue.
ritualTimingAndInterruption.interruptionOutcome: Abort before rolling; no transformation or taxonomy change, no historical roll-failure consequence, and no Soul Coin committed. No partial duration resumes; a new attempt requires full duration, fresh prerequisite recheck and fresh disclosure/consent.
ritualTimingAndInterruption.paymentCommit: Immediately after final prerequisite recheck and immediately before the d20 roll.
ritualTimingAndInterruption.newRuleNotice: Every duration, scheduling, interruption and recheck detail in this object is NEW and requires explicit owner review. It does not claim existing Mage sources establish these mechanics.

preservedOriginals.verbatim: LICH TRANSFORMATION READINESS. At Mage level 10 a character may select Lich only after obtaining either one Soul Coin or two ritual participants, binding at least two named mini-bosses as guardians, securing a planar nexus and surviving the Director's divine-echo encounter. A third bound guardian grants +2 to the final ritual check. If both ritual participants are willing, the final ritual check has advantage.

Before the irreversible Lich roll, the Director must explicitly tell the player the historical failure stakes: permanent loss of spellcasting, transformation into a cursed melee undead NPC, hostile faction consequences, cursed-gear restriction and no further XP as that retired PC. The player must explicitly opt into that retirement risk before rolling. If the player declines, the ritual stops before the roll and the character must choose another Hero path for this playtest; no irreversible consequence is applied.

LICH RITUAL CHECK. After all readiness gates and the divine-echo encounter are completed, roll d20 + Intelligence modifier + Constitution modifier against DC 20, applying the third-guardian +2 and willing-participant advantage where applicable. Success completes the Lich transformation and unlocks its cards and elite companions. Failure after explicit consent applies the historical failure state and the Director pauses for the agreed player-to-NPC handoff before continuing play. No silent PC deletion is permitted.

Success completes the Lich transformation and unlocks its cards and elite companions. At Mage 10 choose Archmage, Elementalist or, if its ritual succeeds, Lich; choose 2 cards from that Hero path. Levels 11, 13, 15, 17 and 19 each grant one eligible unselected Base or Arch choice. Levels 12, 14, 16 and 18 each grant one Hero-path choice. Mage 20 grants one additional Hero-path choice plus the NEW playtest level-20 class capstone in extra Cards. No historical Hero Finale is implied. ASI/feat milestones remain separate.

All acquisition gates use Mage class level, not total character level. Proficiency bonus remains the normal total-character proficiency bonus. Non-Mage levels do not unlock Elemental Focus, Arcanist, Hero cards, Nuke Chain upgrades, Lich ritual access or the level-20 Mage capstone.

Class-spell ranks are printed in the normalized card data: use the legal maximum Mage rank at that card's minimum class level, capped 9; the three Focus finishers are rank 1. Rank determines Dissonance, Counterspell and rank-limited interactions, not a second RP cost. A shared spell uses the ally's normal Action and caster-side Dissonance at the moment it is cast; it never builds the Mage's Nuke Chain remotely. Spellcasting through Fracture as Lich uses the shared direct-trauma rule.
